title: Review: Eukaryotic cell ultrastructure; Membrane structure (fluid mosaic); Protein secretion and the endomembrane system; Cell theory, microscopes and magnification
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE01b#t1 term and clue written for the game; MB01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE01b#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE01a#N.12, CE01b#N.5, MB01a#N.3a, MB01b#N.13, CE01a#N.6, CE01b#N.12, MB01a#N.10a, CE01a#N.9, CE01b#N.2, MB01a#N.7. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Magnification
items.clue: Image size divided by actual size; written with no unit, e.g. ×2000

items.label: Resolution
items.clue: The smallest distance between two points that can still be seen as separate

items.label: Phospholipid
items.clue: Molecule with a charged, water-loving head and two non-polar fatty acid tails.

items.label: Scanning electron microscope
items.clue: Sweeps a beam across a metal-coated specimen to build a 3D image of its surface

questions.stem: A micrograph shows a pollen grain 60 mm across. A scale bar on the micrograph is 20 mm long and is labelled 10 µm. What is the actual diameter of the pollen grain?

options.text: 3 µm
30 µm
60 µm
120 µm

questions.explanation: Magnification = 20 000 µm ÷ 10 µm = ×2000. Actual size = 60 000 µm ÷ 2000 = 30 µm.

questions.stem: A student wants to watch living white blood cells engulfing bacteria about 2 µm long. Which choice of microscope, with its reason, is correct?

options.text: A TEM, as its high resolution would show each step of the engulfing in detail.
An SEM, as its 3D image of the surface would show the cell membrane moving live.
A light microscope, as the cells stay alive and 2 µm is well above its limit.
A light microscope, as extra stain would make the small bacteria appear sharper.

questions.explanation: Living cells can be watched, and bacteria 2 µm long are about ten times larger than the 200 nm resolution limit, so they are clearly resolved.

questions.stem: Why do phospholipids form a bilayer when they are mixed with water?

options.text: Enzymes in the cell join the phospholipids together into a sheet, using energy released from ATP.
The whole molecule repels water, so the phospholipids gather away from it as a droplet of oil.
Covalent bonds form between neighbouring phospholipids, linking them into one rigid sheet of molecules.
Hydrophilic heads face the water and hydrophobic tails are shielded from it, so the sheet forms spontaneously.

questions.explanation: In water the most stable arrangement is a continuous sheet two molecules thick, heads towards the water on both sides and tails in the middle. It forms with no energy input.

questions.stem: A student claims that proteins in the plasma membrane can move sideways within the membrane. Which observation would best support this claim?

options.text: As the cell grows, the total amount of protein in its plasma membrane increases steadily.
When fluorescent proteins in one small patch are permanently bleached, the patch glows again within a minute.
Micrographs show proteins scattered among the phospholipids rather than forming a separate layer.
Proteins labelled on the outer surface of the plasma membrane are later found inside the cytosol.

questions.stem: In a photomicrograph taken at a magnification of ×2000, a red blood cell measures 15 mm across. What is the actual width of the cell?

options.text: 7.5 µm

questions.explanation: Actual size = 15 mm ÷ 2000 = 0.0075 mm, which is 7.5 µm (1 mm = 1000 µm): the typical diameter of a red blood cell.

questions.stem: A virus particle is about 100 nm across. A student photographs a stained sample through a light microscope at ×1500, then enlarges the photo 20 times: a total magnification of ×30 000. At this magnification a 100 nm particle would be 3 mm across. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: Its shape will be visible, as anything 3 mm across in a photo can be seen by eye.
Its shape will be visible if more stain is added to make the image sharper.
Its shape will be visible with a higher-power objective instead of enlarging the photo.
No shape will be seen: the particle is below the 200 nm limit, so enlarging only enlarges blur.

questions.stem: A student draws a two-dimensional representation of the fluid mosaic model. Which feature of the drawing is correct?

options.text: The tails of the inner layer point into the cytoplasm, as the cytoplasm is the inside of the cell.
The proteins are drawn at regular, equal spacings, like tiles set in a fixed pattern across the sheet.
Glycoproteins are drawn with their carbohydrate chains on the cytoplasmic side of the membrane.
Cholesterol is drawn among the phospholipids within the bilayer, not on its surface.

questions.explanation: Cholesterol sits within the bilayer among the phospholipids. The hydrophilic heads form both surfaces and the hydrophobic tails form the core.

questions.stem: With the ×40 objective lens in place, 40 divisions of an eyepiece graticule line up exactly with 100 µm on a stage micrometer. Using the same objective, a cell spans 44 graticule divisions. What is the actual length of the cell in millimetres?

options.text: 1.1 mm

questions.explanation: 100 µm ÷ 40 = 2.5 µm per division with this objective. 44 × 2.5 µm = 110 µm = 0.11 mm.

questions.stem: Ribosomes are about 25 nm across. They cannot be seen with a light microscope but are clearly visible in electron micrographs. What is the reason?

options.text: Electrons have a far shorter wavelength than light, so the resolution is much higher.
The electron microscope magnifies many more times, so much smaller objects become visible.
Heavy-metal stains used for electron microscopy make small structures much sharper.
Electron microscopes use fluorescent stains that make ribosomes glow in the dark.

questions.explanation: Light limits a light microscope to about 200 nm, so a 25 nm ribosome cannot be resolved; the electron beam's much shorter wavelength gives resolution below 1 nm.

questions.stem: Which statement about glycoproteins in the plasma membrane is correct?

options.text: Their carbohydrate is on the extracellular side and is used in cell recognition and adhesion.
Their carbohydrate is on the cytoplasmic side and is respired when the cell lacks glucose.
Their carbohydrate projects from both faces of the membrane so that either face can be recognised.
They are transport proteins whose carbohydrate forms the channel through which sugars enter the cell.

questions.explanation: Glycoproteins are proteins with a carbohydrate chain attached. The carbohydrate faces outwards, where it works in cell recognition and cell adhesion.
